title: SPI flash (NOR flash) protocol
summary: SPI flash (NOR flash) is accessed via SPI bus. Commands: 0x03 (Read Data), 0x0B (Fast Read), 0x02 (Page Program), 0x20 (Sector Erase 4KB), 0x52 (Block Erase 32KB), 0xD8 (Block Erase 64KB), 0xC7/0x60 (Chip Erase), 0x05 (Read Status Register), 0x01 (Write Status Register), 0x06 (Write Enable), 0x04 (Write Disable), 0x9F (Read JEDEC ID), 0x90 (Read Manufacturer/Device ID). Page size: 256 bytes. Sector size: 4KB. Block size: 32KB/64KB.

structure.meaning: 0x0B + 3-byte address + 1 dummy byte. Returns data at higher speed.
0x02 + 3-byte address + up to 256 bytes data. Writes one page (must erase first).
0x20 + 3-byte address. Erases 4KB sector (sets all bits to 1).
0x05. Returns status register: WIP (write in progress), WEL (write enable latch), BP (block protect), etc.
0x06. Sets WEL bit. Required before program/erase.
0x9F. Returns manufacturer ID (1 byte), device ID (2 bytes), capacity (1 byte).
Minimum write unit. Must erase sector before writing.

ext.example_decoded: SPI flash: Read JEDEC ID command (0x9F)
notes: SPI flash is used for firmware storage (BIOS/UEFI, embedded systems).
SPI flash supports QSPI (Quad SPI) for 4x throughput (4 data lines).
SPI flash has limited write endurance (~100K erase cycles per sector).
SPI flash is non-volatile (retains data without power).
Common manufacturers: Winbond, Macronix, Micron, GigaDevice.
